title: fix(plugin-approvals): answer the schema-read delegate with bounded participant probes and index sys_approval_action
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DU5CHkeh2msc49m4dh6kwEt)_

Fixes #33046

Area-lease pilot #33059, area A3.

## What changes

- `approval-service.ts`: the participant rule's three reads (current approver via `sys_approval_approver`, submitter, already acted by `actor_id` / `acted_as`) now live once, as data, in `participantProbes`. `approverIndexWhere` holds the approver-index filter that `approverRequestIds` also reads.
  - **The approvals door is unchanged.** `visibleRequestIds` runs the same three reads as before, with the same filter, fields, 10000-row window and `SYSTEM_CTX`, in the same order. Only the window warning now names the table.
  - **The schema-read delegate (`servesAnyRequest`) asks an existence question.** Each probe fetches at most one row (`limit: 1`). A hit is confirmed by one `limit: 1` read of its request in the caller's organization. The delegate never collects id windows and never builds a request-id `$in`. Here the already-acted probe is scoped on the action row's own `organization_id`, which every writer stamps from the request. Errors behave as before: a failed probe reads as "no", logged, and a failed request read propagates.
- `sys-approval-action.object.ts`: adds indexes `(actor_id, organization_id)` and `(acted_as, organization_id)`, the same shape as `sys_approval_approver`'s `(approver, organization_id)`.
- `approver-address-readers.test.ts` / `approver-address.ts`: the slot-address census and the reader roster now classify the moved sites under `participantProbes` / `approverIndexWhere`. The census also pins that both read shapes (`visibleRequestIds`, `servesAnyRequest`) call `participantProbes`, so the rule cannot fork.

## Why

Since the schema-read delegate landed, every hidden-object list read by a member who cannot read the approval objects ran the door's id-collecting probe. That probe could read up to three 10000-row windows, one of them an unindexed scan of `sys_approval_action`, and then ran one `$in`. The cost grew with the approval history, and the only question being asked was yes or no.

The answer is the same as before. Two edge cases differ. A member whose participation lay past one of the old windows is now admitted, where the window used to hide it. A decision row whose `organization_id` disagrees with its request's is judged by its own column, which is the state the organization backfill repairs.

## Verification

All runs were on head `5e078a77` (fix `d37f3e76`).

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck` + `vitest run` (the whole package, under the verify lock): `Test Files 119 passed (119)`, `Tests 1636 passed (1636)`, `check:test-typecheck: OK`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- New pins (`approval-service.test.ts`, `bounded probe`): an engine spy checks that every approval-table read has `limit <= 1` and that none has an `id: { $in }` filter. The same tests check the yes/no answer for:
  - the pending approver and the submitter;
  - a past actor (by `actor_id`) and a slot holder (by `acted_as`);
  - a non-participant, and one holding a different position;
  - a past actor in another organization (no) and in their own (yes);
  - an orphaned decision (no).
  
  A further test checks that the two indexes are declared.
- **Ablation, run once on committed `d37f3e76`:** `servesAnyRequest` was swapped back to the pre-fix body (`visibleRequestIds` + `$in`) with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The mutation landed (`anchor 1 -> 0, blob 5df478ba2510 -> 9f53ed0779af`). Result: `Tests 4 failed | 484 passed (488)`.
  - Three `bounded probe` tests failed with `sys_approval_approver read is bounded: expected 10000 to be less than or equal to 1`.
  - The census test failed with `servesAnyRequest ... to match /this\.participantProbes\(who, tenantOrg\)/`.
  - The verdict assertions, which run before the bounded check, passed on the old code too, so the answer is unchanged.
  - Restored with `git checkout HEAD`: `blob == HEAD (5df478ba2510) and git diff HEAD is empty`.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 5 touched sources: exit 0.
- Derived gates, run locally, all exit 0: `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` (1 non-breaking changeset), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-issue-citations`, `check-tenant-audit-census`, `check-comment-mask-adoption`, `check:platform-object-tenancy-census`, `check:system-context-census`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:objectql-double-limit`, `check:where-matcher`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:object-def-param-keys`, `check:org-identifier`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:i18n`. It exits 3 with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` because the CLI is not built in this worktree. This diff changes no label. CI runs the rest of the farm.
